scenes.heading: EXT. NORTH ATLANTIC / WRECK SITE — DAY (1996)
scenes.summary: A deep-sea expedition maps the wreck and finds a portrait that brings an elderly witness back to 1912.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The search begins where memory went down.

beats.title: SONAR GRID
beats.text: The research vessel sweeps a sonar grid across the seabed.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Steel leaves a shadow long after voices leave.

beats.title: DESCENT
beats.text: A submersible drops through black water toward the liner’s broken bow.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Below the surface, time has no shoreline.

beats.title: WRECK
beats.text: The remote camera passes torn corridors, china, and a silent grand staircase.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Every object keeps the shape of the hand that used it.

beats.title: SAFE
beats.text: A robotic arm opens a battered safe and lifts a damp sketch case.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The ocean gives back one small witness.

beats.title: PORTRAIT
beats.text: A charcoal portrait appears on the monitor; the elderly Rose claims the young woman.
beats.narration: ROSE: That is me, before the ship became a story.

scenes.heading: INT. KELDYSH — DAY (1996)
scenes.summary: On the research ship, Rose identifies herself and turns a treasure hunt into a complete memory of Titanic.
scenes.narration: ROSE: You are looking for a jewel; I remember a life.

beats.title: NAME
beats.text: Rose Calvert watches the salvage team search the safe for the Heart of the Ocean.
beats.narration: ROSE: My name was Rose DeWitt Bukater then.

beats.title: DRAWING
beats.text: The crew studies the dated drawing and compares it with the wreck footage.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: A face crosses a century intact.

beats.title: DIAMOND
beats.text: Brock presses Rose for the diamond’s last known location.
beats.narration: BROCK: The stone was on the ship.

beats.title: MEMORY
beats.text: Rose looks from the monitor to the sea and begins describing Southampton.
beats.narration: ROSE: It was called the Ship of Dreams.

beats.title: TRANSITION
beats.text: The modern ocean dissolves into a crowded dock in April 1912.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Her memory opens at the moment of departure.

scenes.heading: INT. ROSE’S BEDROOM — NIGHT (1912)
scenes.summary: Young Rose prepares for the maiden voyage while family duty turns her future into an arrangement.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: Before the ship moves, a life is already being steered.

beats.title: DRESS
beats.text: Maids lace Rose into a corset while trunks are closed around her.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Silk can feel like a restraint when every seam is watched.

beats.title: MOTHER
beats.text: Ruth explains that the family’s money and name depend on Rose’s marriage.
beats.narration: RUTH: A daughter of our name has obligations.

beats.title: CAL
beats.text: Caledon Hockley offers a jewel and speaks of their engagement as settled.
beats.narration: CAL: The future is already waiting for us.

beats.title: WINDOW
beats.text: Rose looks down at ordinary travelers and imagines the street outside.
beats.narration: ROSE: Everyone down there seems to know where they are going.

beats.title: DEPART
beats.text: The family carriage leaves for the docks beneath a grey sky.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The road to Titanic narrows behind her.

scenes.heading: EXT. SOUTHAMPTON DOCKS — DAY (1912)
scenes.summary: Passengers crowd the quay as Titanic prepares to sail; Jack wins a last-minute passage and boards with steerage.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: A city gathers around one impossible machine.

beats.title: ARRIVAL
beats.text: First-class cars and third-class carts converge on the enormous dock.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Class divides the queue before the ship divides the sea.

beats.title: JACK
beats.text: Jack Dawson wins passage in a card game and runs toward the gangway.
beats.narration: JACK: We have got a ship to catch.

beats.title: WHISTLE
beats.text: Titanic’s hull rises above the dock while crewmen move beneath it.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The ship looks less built than announced.

beats.title: DECK
beats.text: Steerage passengers are counted, searched, and directed below.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The same voyage begins through different doors.

beats.title: SAIL
beats.text: Mooring lines fall and Southampton slides away from the stern.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: At last, the world starts moving backward.

scenes.heading: INT. THIRD-CLASS CABIN / DECK — DAY
scenes.summary: Jack finds friends among the steerage passengers and begins drawing the people and machinery around him.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: Below the polished rooms, the voyage is loud, close, and alive.

beats.title: CABIN
beats.text: Jack stows his bag beside Fabrizio’s bunk in a crowded cabin.
beats.narration: FABRIZIO: We will make this ship remember us.

beats.title: FRIENDS
beats.text: Tommy introduces Jack to the rough jokes and quick alliances of steerage.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Friendship arrives before luggage is unpacked.

beats.title: DECK
beats.text: Passengers cheer as Titanic gathers speed beyond the harbour.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Everyone measures freedom by how fast the land disappears.

beats.title: BOW
beats.text: Jack sketches faces, hands, and the hard geometry of the ship.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: He records strangers before they know they matter.

beats.title: NIGHTFALL
beats.text: Electric lights bloom across the decks as open water surrounds the liner.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Night turns the ship into its own small city.

scenes.heading: INT. FIRST-CLASS SUITE — DAY
scenes.summary: Rose is dressed for a first-class life while Ruth and Cal turn the voyage into a public rehearsal for marriage.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: Upstairs, comfort hides the pressure it was built to protect.

beats.title: CORSET
beats.text: Ruth supervises Rose’s dress and corrects every detail of her posture.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: A perfect silhouette leaves little room to breathe.

beats.title: ETIQUETTE
beats.text: Molly Brown offers Rose practical advice beneath the formal rules.
beats.narration: MOLLY: There is more than one way to survive a dinner.

beats.title: GIFT
beats.text: Cal presents the Heart of the Ocean as proof of ownership and affection.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The diamond shines brightest when no one asks what it costs.

beats.title: ENGAGEMENT
beats.text: Ruth treats the wedding as a family rescue plan rather than a choice.
beats.narration: RUTH: We are both being practical.

beats.title: TRAP
beats.text: Rose studies her reflection and feels the suite close around her.
beats.narration: ROSE: I can see the whole of my life, and I do not want it.

scenes.heading: INT. FIRST-CLASS DINING SALON — EVENING
scenes.summary: The first-class table celebrates speed and status while Rose performs the role everyone has chosen for her.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The chandeliers hold a dinner above a dangerous silence.

beats.title: TABLE
beats.text: Servants place silver and crystal as the guests take their seats.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Every place setting marks a place in the order.

beats.title: ISMAY
beats.text: J. Bruce Ismay praises Titanic’s speed and the attention it commands.
beats.narration: ISMAY: The maiden voyage must be remembered.

beats.title: CAL
beats.text: Cal corrects Rose’s table manners while speaking for her.
beats.narration: CAL: A lady does not need to explain herself.

beats.title: MOLLY
beats.text: Molly Brown punctures the performance with a joke and a new perspective.
beats.narration: MOLLY: Let the girl finish her own sentence.

beats.title: STARES
beats.text: Rose leaves the table smiling for the room and empty for herself.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Applause can sound like another locked door.

scenes.heading: EXT. STERN — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Rose walks to the stern intending to end her life; Jack finds her and gives her a reason to climb back.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: At the edge of the ship, one choice can change the entire map.

beats.title: WALK
beats.text: Rose crosses empty corridors and reaches the cold stern deck alone.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The ship keeps moving while she stands outside her future.

beats.title: RAILING
beats.text: She climbs over the stern rail and looks down at the black water.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The sea is close enough to answer.

beats.title: JACK
beats.text: Jack sees her, talks about the drop, and asks her to look back at him.
beats.narration: JACK: Do not let go. Look at me.

beats.title: RESCUE
beats.text: Jack pulls Rose over the rail as crewmen rush toward the commotion.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Her first rescue is also their first connection.

beats.title: DEAL
beats.text: Rose protects Jack from blame, and Cal offers him a place at dinner.
beats.narration: CAL: A debt of gratitude can be repaid at my table.

scenes.heading: INT. FIRST-CLASS CORRIDOR — NIGHT
scenes.summary: The rescue becomes a social transaction as Cal, Lovejoy, and Rose decide what Jack’s presence will mean.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: A private rescue is rewritten by the people who witnessed it.

beats.title: REPORT
beats.text: Rose’s maid reports the incident while Ruth listens for scandal.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The story reaches the drawing room before Rose does.

beats.title: CAL
beats.text: Cal questions Jack and measures him against the rules of the ship.
beats.narration: CAL: Courage is not the same as belonging.

beats.title: LOVEJOY
beats.text: Spicer Lovejoy searches Jack for a motive behind the rescue.
beats.narration: LOVEJOY: Everyone wants something.

beats.title: THANKS
beats.text: Rose tells Jack she owes him her life, not an explanation.
beats.narration: ROSE: You saw me as a person.

beats.title: INVITE
beats.text: Cal insists Jack attend dinner in first class under his supervision.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The invitation is a leash dressed as courtesy.

scenes.heading: INT. FIRST-CLASS DINING SALON — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Jack joins Cal’s table and answers the class test with a life shaped by travel, work, and observation.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The room asks Jack to prove he deserves to breathe its air.

beats.title: ARRIVAL
beats.text: Jack enters in borrowed clothes while every face turns toward him.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: A borrowed coat cannot hide a real life.

beats.title: TEST
beats.text: The guests ask where he studied, what he owns, and who will vouch for him.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Questions become fences when answers are ranked.

beats.title: ART
beats.text: Jack describes seeing the world and drawing people instead of collecting possessions.
beats.narration: JACK: I keep moving; I keep looking.

beats.title: ROSE
beats.text: Rose watches him make room for possibility at a table built from certainty.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Her escape begins as attention.

beats.title: UNEASE
beats.text: Cal smiles across the table while Lovejoy studies Jack’s hands.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Control notices freedom before freedom notices itself.

scenes.heading: INT. GRAND STAIRCASE / PROMENADE — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Rose slips away from the formal party and meets Jack between the grand staircase and the open deck.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The ship has two nights, and Rose starts walking between them.

beats.title: ESCAPE
beats.text: Rose leaves the dinner before dessert and descends toward the public corridors.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Her footsteps become her first unscripted sentence.

beats.title: DECK
beats.text: Jack catches her under the lifeboat davits and offers the view beyond the rail.
beats.narration: JACK: You do not have to stay where they put you.

beats.title: SKETCHES
beats.text: Rose discovers Jack’s drawings and sees his attention as a kind of respect.
beats.narration: ROSE: You look at people without asking them to perform.

beats.title: TURN
beats.text: She crosses from the polished promenade toward the music below.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: A doorway becomes a border she chooses to cross.

beats.title: MUSIC
beats.text: Steerage music rises through the stairwell as Rose follows it downstairs.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The ship’s heartbeat is louder below.

scenes.heading: INT. THIRD-CLASS PARTY — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Rose joins the steerage celebration, finding movement, laughter, and a version of herself that Cal cannot choreograph.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: In the lower rooms, joy does not ask for a ticket.

beats.title: WELCOME
beats.text: Tommy raises a glass as Jack brings Rose into the crowded room.
beats.narration: TOMMY: Tonight, everyone gets the same floor.

beats.title: DANCE
beats.text: Rose tries the fast steps and lets the music pull her out of posture.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Her body remembers freedom before her mind approves it.

beats.title: LAUGH
beats.text: Jack and Rose laugh when exhaustion turns the dance into a stumble.
beats.narration: ROSE: I have never been this tired.

beats.title: WATCH
beats.text: Lovejoy learns that Rose has left the first-class party.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Somewhere above, the search for her has already begun.

beats.title: CHASE
beats.text: Rose races back toward the upper decks before the night can expose them.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The secret returns upstairs with wet shoes and a pulse.

scenes.heading: EXT. BOW — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Jack brings Rose to the bow, where the horizon, wind, and their first kiss give her a new sense of scale.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The front of the ship feels like the front of a life.

beats.title: MEET
beats.text: Rose finds Jack waiting at the prow after slipping away from her chaperone.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Their private place is made from open water.

beats.title: HORIZON
beats.text: They speak about the places Jack has seen and the choices Rose has not made.
beats.narration: JACK: The horizon is wider than this ship.

beats.title: RAIL
beats.text: Jack guides Rose’s hands to the rail and steadies her against the wind.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Trust begins as balance.

beats.title: WINGS
beats.text: Rose opens her arms over the bow and feels the ship carry her forward.
beats.narration: ROSE: I can see everything now.

beats.title: KISS
beats.text: They kiss while Titanic cuts a bright line through the dark sea.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: A small decision becomes impossible to hide from them.

scenes.heading: INT. ROSE’S SUITE — DAY
scenes.summary: Rose invites Jack to draw her wearing the Heart of the Ocean, turning a stolen hour into a record of her choice.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The portrait is commissioned by a woman choosing how she will be seen.

beats.title: RETURN
beats.text: Rose brings Jack into the suite while the family is elsewhere on the ship.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Every quiet corridor carries a risk.

beats.title: POSE
beats.text: She asks Jack to draw her without the manners and clothes that define her.
beats.narration: ROSE: Draw me as the person I am trying to become.

beats.title: DIAMOND
beats.text: The Heart of the Ocean rests at her throat as she settles before the sketchbook.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The jewel becomes evidence, not decoration.

beats.title: SKETCH
beats.text: Jack draws while Rose holds his gaze and refuses to look away.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The line of a pencil makes a private promise visible.

beats.title: STAMP
beats.text: Jack dates the portrait and Rose hides it among her belongings.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: One image survives because someone chose to keep it.

scenes.heading: INT. ROSE’S SUITE / CORRIDOR — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Cal discovers the portrait and sends Lovejoy after Rose and Jack as the romance becomes an open threat.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The room that held a secret becomes the room that exposes it.

beats.title: DISCOVER
beats.text: Cal opens Rose’s sketch case and finds the drawing beside the jewel.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Paper can cut deeper than a confession.

beats.title: RAGE
beats.text: He tears through the room and demands that Rose return to her role.
beats.narration: CAL: You will not make a fool of me.

beats.title: DIAMOND
beats.text: Rose refuses to apologize for wanting a life that belongs to her.
beats.narration: ROSE: I am not a possession.

beats.title: LOVEJOY
beats.text: Cal orders Lovejoy to find the couple and bring Rose back.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The chase begins behind polished doors.

beats.title: RUN
beats.text: Rose and Jack escape down service stairs toward the cargo hold.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Their route leaves first class and enters the machinery of survival.

scenes.heading: INT. CARGO HOLD — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Rose and Jack hide among the automobiles, choosing intimacy while Lovejoy searches the dark hold around them.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: Beneath the ballroom, metal and breath become a private room.

beats.title: HOLD
beats.text: Jack leads Rose between crates and covered cars in the dim cargo deck.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The ship stores its wealth below the people who own it.

beats.title: RENAULT
beats.text: He opens the door of a Renault and gives Rose a moment without witnesses.
beats.narration: JACK: For a minute, let the ship belong to nobody.

beats.title: CHOICE
beats.text: Rose closes the car door on Cal’s world and stays with Jack.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Consent becomes the clearest line in the scene.

beats.title: WINDOW
beats.text: Their breath fogs the glass as the car rocks with the moving hull.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The ocean writes a temporary mark on the window.

beats.title: FOOTSTEPS
beats.text: Lovejoy passes close by; the couple remains hidden until the hold is quiet.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Danger walks past without seeing the future it carries.

scenes.heading: INT. BRIDGE / LOOKOUT — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Lookouts spot an iceberg, the bridge orders a turn, and Titanic strikes the ice beneath the calm surface.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The revision point is not the collision alone; it is every line that now has to move.

beats.title: WATCH
beats.text: Lookouts scan a flat, moonlit sea while the bridge keeps the liner on course.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Calm water can conceal a wall.

beats.title: ICE
beats.text: A dark mass resolves ahead; the warning bell breaks the bridge routine.
beats.narration: LOOKOUT: Iceberg, dead ahead.

beats.title: ORDER
beats.text: Murdoch orders the engines reversed and the helm hard over.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: A command travels faster than a ship can turn.

beats.title: SCRAPE
beats.text: Titanic’s hull meets the iceberg below the waterline and compartments begin to flood.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The damage is quiet enough to be misunderstood.

beats.title: SILENCE
beats.text: The ship shudders; passengers wake without yet knowing the shape of the danger.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Every story after this moment inherits the impact.

scenes.heading: INT. LOWER DECKS / STEERAGE CORRIDORS — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Water enters the lower decks while officers calculate the damage and steerage passengers meet locked gates and confusing routes.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The first people to feel the sinking are the people furthest from the boats.

beats.title: ALARM
beats.text: Officers inspect the damaged compartments and send runners through the ship.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Information arrives as fragments before it becomes an order.

beats.title: WATER
beats.text: The mail room and boiler spaces take on water behind closing doors.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Steel doors delay the sea but cannot negotiate with it.

beats.title: GATES
beats.text: Steerage passengers reach barriers and search for a route upward.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: A map designed for class becomes a trap.

beats.title: CALCULATION
beats.text: Thomas Andrews traces the flooding and estimates the remaining time.
beats.narration: ANDREWS: The ship cannot stay afloat.

beats.title: DANGER
beats.text: The warning reaches upper decks while the lower corridors grow harder to cross.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The timetable is now measured in rooms filling with water.

scenes.heading: INT. FIRST-CLASS SUITE / CORRIDOR — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Rose and Jack return to the changing ship; Cal discovers the diamond and frames Jack before the evacuation.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The old order keeps fighting even after the ship proves it cannot protect anyone.

beats.title: RETURN
beats.text: Rose and Jack emerge from the cargo hold into corridors filled with questions.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Their private escape ends in a public emergency.

beats.title: CAL
beats.text: Cal sees Rose with Jack and hides panic beneath an order to return to the suite.
beats.narration: CAL: Stay with me and you will be safe.

beats.title: COAT
beats.text: Cal retrieves the Heart of the Ocean and slips it into a coat near Jack.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: A jewel becomes a weapon in a single pocket.

beats.title: FRAME
beats.text: Lovejoy points officers toward Jack and supplies a story that sounds official.
beats.narration: LOVEJOY: The evidence is on him.

beats.title: ARREST
beats.text: Jack is handcuffed and taken below while Rose is directed toward the lifeboats.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The revision now changes both the romance and the escape path.

scenes.heading: EXT. BOAT DECK / GRAND STAIRCASE — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Lifeboats begin launching as Rose is separated from Jack, then refuses safety when she realizes he is still trapped.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: A seat in a boat is offered as if survival can be assigned.

beats.title: BOATS
beats.text: Women and children are loaded while officers count places and lower the first boats.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The deck becomes a ledger of who is allowed to leave.

beats.title: CAL
beats.text: Cal promises Rose a future while concealing the truth about Jack’s arrest.
beats.narration: CAL: There is room for you beside me.

beats.title: LOOKBACK
beats.text: From the boat, Rose sees Jack missing and understands the story Cal has manufactured.
beats.narration: ROSE: Where is he?

beats.title: CHOICE
beats.text: Rose steps away from the lifeboat and runs back toward the sinking ship.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The safest decision is not the decision she can live with.

beats.title: RETURN
beats.text: She crosses the grand staircase as water rises through the lower levels.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Love becomes an upstream route through the disaster.

scenes.heading: INT. FLOODED MASTER-AT-ARMS OFFICE — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Rose finds Jack handcuffed in a flooding office, breaks the chain, and leads them through the rising corridors.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The rescue reverses direction; the person saved becomes the person who saves.

beats.title: SEARCH
beats.text: Rose follows signs and echoes toward the holding room below deck.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Every corridor is now a question with a closing door.

beats.title: WATER
beats.text: Jack calls from behind the bars as water reaches the office floor.
beats.narration: JACK: Rose, I am here.

beats.title: AXE
beats.text: Rose finds an emergency axe and raises it with both hands.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Fear is still present; it simply has a task.

beats.title: BREAK
beats.text: She strikes the chain and frees Jack from the handcuffs.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: One cut restores the line between them.

beats.title: ESCAPE
beats.text: They swim through a corridor as doors buckle and the lights fail overhead.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The ship’s interior becomes an ocean of its own.

scenes.heading: EXT. BOAT DECK / COLLAPSING SHIP — NIGHT
scenes.summary: Rose and Jack move through the evacuation as Cal fires after them and Titanic’s stern begins to rise.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The last open deck is shrinking beneath every choice.

beats.title: BOATS
beats.text: They reach the boat deck where launches continue under shouted orders.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: There are too few boats for the scale of the night.

beats.title: CAL
beats.text: Cal returns with a gun and claims the diamond will buy a place in the next boat.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Wealth survives only as long as someone believes it can.

beats.title: JACK
beats.text: Rose rejects Cal’s promise and stays with Jack at the rail.
beats.narration: ROSE: I am not getting on without you.

beats.title: COLLAPSE
beats.text: The stern lifts and the musicians keep playing as passengers search for higher ground.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Music gives panic a rhythm it cannot stop.

beats.title: GUN
beats.text: Cal fires; Rose and Jack run toward the rising stern while the crowd breaks apart.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The route forward is now vertical.

scenes.heading: INT. GRAND STAIRCASE / EXT. STERN — NIGHT
scenes.summary: The hull tears apart, passengers slide into the sea, and Rose and Jack cling to the stern as Titanic disappears beneath them.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The ship’s final movement carries everyone beyond the old map.

beats.title: STAIRCASE
beats.text: Water climbs the grand staircase while glass, furniture, and people move together.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The symbol of order becomes a river.

beats.title: RUN
beats.text: Jack and Rose climb across decks toward the highest end of the ship.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Every step is taken on a structure already failing.

beats.title: BREAK
beats.text: The hull splits and the lights vanish as the bow drops away.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The impossible ship finally separates from itself.

beats.title: FALL
beats.text: Passengers slide down the rising stern into the black Atlantic.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Gravity finishes what the iceberg began.

beats.title: STERN
beats.text: Rose and Jack hold the rail as the stern points into the sky.
beats.narration: JACK: Stay with me.

scenes.heading: EXT. NORTH ATLANTIC — NIGHT
scenes.summary: In the freezing water, Rose and Jack share a floating panel, promise a future, and wait for a lifeboat to return.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: Survival becomes a space barely large enough for one body and one promise.

beats.title: WRECKAGE
beats.text: The wreck scatters debris and survivors across the dark water.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The sea removes every distinction the ship enforced.

beats.title: PANEL
beats.text: Rose climbs onto a floating panel while Jack stays beside her in the water.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: A door becomes a raft because there is nothing else.

beats.title: PROMISE
beats.text: Jack keeps Rose awake and makes her promise to continue living.
beats.narration: JACK: You will build a life beyond this night.

beats.title: DISTANCE
beats.text: A lifeboat rows away, then turns after Rose’s voice reaches the survivors.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The smallest sound can redirect the rescue.

beats.title: WHISTLE
beats.text: Rose finds the officer’s whistle and calls until the lifeboat sees her.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Her voice is the last signal between memory and morning.

scenes.heading: EXT. CARPATHIA / NEW YORK / ROSE’S MEMORY — DAWN/NIGHT
scenes.summary: Rose is rescued, chooses her own name, survives into old age, and returns the diamond to the ocean before finding Titanic alive in memory.
scenes.narration: NARRATOR: The ending is not the sinking; it is the life Rose carries away.

beats.title: RESCUE
beats.text: Carpathia reaches the survivors and lifts Rose from the freezing sea.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: Dawn counts the living without explaining the missing.

beats.title: NAME
beats.text: On the rescue ship, Rose refuses Cal’s name and chooses to introduce herself anew.
beats.narration: ROSE: I will say my own name.

beats.title: NEW YORK
beats.text: She steps onto the New York dock alone, carrying grief and the possibility of work, travel, and change.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: A life begins in the space the ship could not close.

beats.title: DIAMOND
beats.text: Decades later, elderly Rose releases the Heart of the Ocean over the dark water.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The treasure returns to the place that kept the truth.

beats.title: REUNION
beats.text: Rose dies peacefully and imagines the Titanic’s grand staircase filled with the people she loved.
beats.narration: NARRATOR: The final map is memory, and everyone is waiting there.
